Overhead Lines
Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: TL-041-r0a
Equipment: Overhead lines
Issued to: Transmission and Distribution
Status: Approved
Approval date: 28 August 2005
Procedure: Fitting dead-end clamps for steel-reinforced aluminium conductors (ACSR)
Next review date: August 2010

sections_en.text: This document sets out the steps for compressing dead-end clamps for steel-reinforced aluminium conductors (ACSR) on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.

The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

rows: A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards.
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc.
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc.

Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression.
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc.
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them.
Make sure the dies for aluminium and steel represent the required size.
Make sure the inner diameters of the ends (steel, aluminium) are clean.
Make sure the conductor end is sound and cut off damaged ends.
Insert the conductor into the aluminium end and let it slide in about 1 metre.

Bind the conductor with metal wire or suitable adhesive tape about 3 cm from the end, then cut the aluminium ends near the adhesive tape with a hacksaw, taking care not to nick the steel wires (Figure x1a).
Bind the steel conductor ends (Figure x1b).
Bind the conductor cover at a distance from the end equal to: depth (eye end hole + 15%).

Cut the aluminium wires in front of the adhesive tape (Figure x1c), taking into account not nicking the wires; to avoid this, cut with the saw the outer layers of the cover, cut only 2/3 of the inner diameter of the aluminium wire layers to be cut by repeated bending.

Put a mark on the core from which the aluminium wires have been removed, at a distance equal to the depth of the eye end hole. Insert the core 2 cm into the steel end, then remove the cover (the adhesive tape), then, using pliers, insert the core and make sure it has been inserted up to the mark made previously; to carry out this operation easily, hold the steel end by gently compressing it with the dies fixed on the press.

Compress the cylindrical part of the steel end starting from the printed mark (Figure x1d) and continue compressing towards the conductor until it overlaps by half a compression with each following compression (over lapping one half of each comp), making sure of the appropriate pressure value shown on the pressure gauge.

Clean all the aluminium wires of the conductor in the part to be compressed; if there is grease or blackening, use a suitable solvent, and in the other case use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.

Insert the aluminium dead-end joint into the steel end after removing the adhesive tape, until the polygonal shapes are inserted into each other. Make sure of the correct direction of the steel end relative to the direction of the terminal end (Figure x1d).
Compress the first part of the aluminium dead-end joint, specifically towards the steel end (Figure x1f), starting from the mark made, so that it overlaps by half as shown in step (10).
Compress the second part of the end starting from the mark made, then continue compressing towards the conductor (Figure x1g) and continue working as in steps (10) & (13).
Clean carefully all the aluminium wires at the end of the conductor, exactly as shown in step (11), which will be inserted into the bridle lug.
Insert the conductor into the bridle lug, then start compressing from the terminal end side (Figure x1h), then continue as previously shown.
Make sure the contact surfaces of the terminal end and the bridle lug are clean by cleaning with cloth, then finally tie the two parts together.

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for compressing dead-end clamps for steel-reinforced aluminium conductors (ACSR) on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.
The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions
A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards. | 
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc. | 
The following shall be observed:
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc. | 
Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the sleeve shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression. | 
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc. | 
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation. | 
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
Make sure the dies for aluminium and steel represent the required size. | 1.
Make sure the inner diameters of the ends (steel, aluminium) are clean. | 2.
Make sure the conductor end is sound and cut off damaged ends. | 3.
Insert the conductor into the aluminium end and let it slide in about 1 metre. | 4.
Bind the conductor with metal wire or suitable adhesive tape about 3 cm from the end, then cut the aluminium ends near the adhesive tape with a hacksaw, taking care not to nick the steel wires (Figure x1a). | 5.
Bind the steel conductor ends (Figure x1b). | 6.
Bind the conductor cover at a distance from the end equal to: depth (eye end hole + 15%). | 7.
Cut the aluminium wires in front of the adhesive tape (Figure x1c), taking into account not nicking the wires; to avoid this, cut with the saw the outer layers of the cover, cut only 2/3 of the inner diameter of the aluminium wire layers to be cut by repeated bending. | 8.
Put a mark on the core from which the aluminium wires have been removed, at a distance equal to the depth of the eye end hole. Insert the core 2 cm into the steel end, then remove the cover (the adhesive tape), then, using pliers, insert the core and make sure it has been inserted up to the mark made previously; to carry out this operation easily, hold the steel end by gently compressing it with the dies fixed on the press. | 9.
Compress the cylindrical part of the steel end starting from the printed mark (Figure x1d) and continue compressing towards the conductor until it overlaps by half a compression with each following compression (over lapping one half of each comp), making sure of the appropriate pressure value shown on the pressure gauge. | 10.
Clean all the aluminium wires of the conductor in the part to be compressed; if there is grease or blackening, use a suitable solvent, and in the other case use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long. | 11.
Insert the aluminium dead-end joint into the steel end after removing the adhesive tape, until the polygonal shapes are inserted into each other. Make sure of the correct direction of the steel end relative to the direction of the terminal end (Figure x1d). | 12.
Compress the first part of the aluminium dead-end joint, specifically towards the steel end (Figure x1f), starting from the mark made, so that it overlaps by half as shown in step (10). | 13.
Compress the second part of the end starting from the mark made, then continue compressing towards the conductor (Figure x1g) and continue working as in steps (10) & (13). | 14.
Clean carefully all the aluminium wires at the end of the conductor, exactly as shown in step (11), which will be inserted into the bridle lug. | 15.
Insert the conductor into the bridle lug, then start compressing from the terminal end side (Figure x1h), then continue as previously shown. | 16.
Make sure the contact surfaces of the terminal end and the bridle lug are clean by cleaning with cloth, then finally tie the two parts together. | 17.
